`[name, kind, index, columns]` written with `separators=(",", ":")` and
`ensure_ascii=False`: `name` the table's name (below), `kind` one of
`place`, `rule`, `census`, `row` and `chain` (the last three RESERVED
for lanes MG and L3), `index` the step's number (for `rule`, the rule's
identity, the array `[kind, computed, inputs]` of 4.6b.5), and `columns`
the eligible columns'
names in schema order (for `rule`, the columns eligible before any rule
step). The word is never keyed by a per-project key, the table's content
or its content hash (ruling R6 as amended 2026-10-18).

**The table's name** is the person's name for the dataset: by default
the input file's name without its extension, or `--name NAME`. It is not
secret. Two different tables described under different names take
independent words; the same table under one name and one key, with the
same settings, the same answers in the questions file and the same
`procedure` constants, takes the same words, so a re-profile publishes
the same description byte for byte. An answer that changes which columns
are eligible (one that ends a hold, plan P4-D401) changes every word,
the eligible columns being an input: the first review measured 0 of 39
step words equal before and after one column became eligible. Another
floor or another `procedure` constant leaves every word as it was, since
neither is an input, but it can change which options are offered or
eligible and their weights, so the same words can place other options
(Codex's item 16 of 2026-10-19 corrected the first build's "changes
every word" here). Either way the description can differ, and the
ledger below refuses a second, different description.

**The key** is 32 bytes from `secrets.token_bytes`, made by the first
`synthtwin profile` on the installation and kept in the installation's
DATA FOLDER: a folder private to the user's account (mode 0700 on POSIX,
the key file 0600; on Windows under the user's own local
application-data folder). Lane CHa fixes the folder on each platform and
tests the `os.name == 'nt'` form on every platform. A key file another
account can read or write is refused, in plain words, until it is fixed.
The key is never written into the description, the twin, any log, the
shared report or the private report; the private report names only the
key file's path. The tests use a fixed test key, and no fixture's
expected output depends on any other.

**The key's FINGERPRINT** is keyed BLAKE2b of the bytes `b"key
fingerprint"` under the key, `digest_size=8`,
`person=b"synthtwin.kfp.1"`: a domain no draw word uses, so a
fingerprint never equals a word.

**The LEDGER** is a file beside the key in the data folder (0600), never
beside a run's output. It holds, for each table described on the
installation, its name, its CONTENT HASH (4.6b.8), the fingerprint of
the key that described it and the DESCRIPTION DIGEST of what that run
published: unkeyed BLAKE2b, `digest_size=32`,
`person=b"synthtwin.desc.1"`, over the PROTECTED PUBLICATION, which is
the whole description as written, in the canonical serialization of
section 3, less only the keys that stamp the run (the producer's
version and any time or path it records; lane CHa lists them from
section 4.1). So another setting, another column block or another chain
each gives another digest, and a description whose `statistical` is
`null` is digested whole too (Codex's item 9 of 2026-10-19: the first
build digested `relationships.statistical` alone, which a floor of 12
against 11 could leave unchanged while the column blocks moved). The
ledger compares two descriptions of one table only where one of them
publishes something between columns (`statistical` not `null`); two
that both publish nothing between columns are the base product's, as
today, and the second is recorded without a refusal. It is read before
anything is published, and its decisions are printed on the screen of
the person who holds the table, never written into the description, the
twin, a log or either report (inventory row 33):
- **the same content, name and key, and the same description:** the run
  proceeds;
- **the same content, name and key, and a DIFFERENT description** (an
  answer in the questions file, a setting or a newer synthtwin changed
  what it would publish): REFUSED: "This table was described before
  under the name '<name>', and this run would publish a different
  description of it (an answer, a setting or a newer version of
  synthtwin changed it). Someone holding both descriptions could narrow
  a small group of patients. If the earlier description was never
  shared with anyone, run again with --replace-description; otherwise
  share only the earlier one.";
- **the same content under another name:** REFUSED: "This table was
  described before under the name '<old>'. Describing it again under
  another name would give a second, different description, and someone
  holding both could narrow a small group of patients. Run again with
  --name <old>.";
- **the same content under another key:** REFUSED: "This table was
  described before with a different private key. Describing it again
  could let someone who holds both descriptions narrow a small group of
  patients. Put the old key file back at <path>; or, if no description
  of this table made with the old key was ever shared, run again with
  --replace-description.";
- **a different content under a name already used:** a one-line warning,
  and the run proceeds: "A different table was described before under
  the name '<name>'. If this is a newer extract of the same table, share
  only one of the two descriptions with the same people; if it is a
  different table, run again with --name and a new name.";
- **a ledger but no readable key file:** REFUSED before anything is
  read: "The private key at <path> is missing, but this installation has
  described tables before. Put the key file back. If it is lost, run
  again with --new-key: each table described before will then be
  refused until you confirm, with --replace-description, that its
  earlier descriptions were never shared.";
- **no ledger and no key** (a new installation, or a deleted data
  folder): a new key is made, and one line says so: "A new private key
  was made at <path>. Keep it: describing the same table again needs the
  same key.";
- **a key file but no ledger** (the ledger deleted or lost): the run
  proceeds, starts a new ledger, and one line says so: "No record of
  earlier descriptions was found beside the private key at <path>, so a
  new record was started. If this installation described tables before,
  describe each again only under its old name." (stated limit 2: a
  deleted ledger);
- **a ledger that cannot be read** (damaged, or written in a form this
  version does not know): REFUSED before anything is read: "The record
  of earlier descriptions at <path> cannot be read. Put back a copy that
  can; or, if no description made on this installation was ever shared,
  move it aside and run again."

**Amended 2026-10-21 (lane CHa, plan P4-D418): the folder and the lock
as built.** The DATA FOLDER is `$XDG_DATA_HOME/synthtwin` where that is
set, else `~/Library/Application Support/synthtwin` on macOS and
`~/.local/share/synthtwin` elsewhere on POSIX, and
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\synthtwin` on Windows (`~\AppData\Local\synthtwin`
where it is unset); it holds `chain-key`, `chain-ledger` (JSON, with no ending: a private
record, never among the files a run leaves beside the twin) and, during
a run, `chain-profile.lock`. The lock is made with `pathlib.Path.touch(...,
exist_ok=False)`, which is `os.open` with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL`; the ledger
entry goes to `chain-ledger.new` and is moved into place with
`pathlib.Path.replace` (`os.replace`). A key file that a group or other
account may read or write is refused on POSIX; on Windows the folder is
the user's own, and no POSIX mode is read. `tests/test_chain_profile.py`
runs every case in both forms.

**One run at a time, and the entry before the description.** A run
holds the installation's LOCK, a file it makes in the data folder with
`os.open` and the flags `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` (standard library, the same
on every platform), from the moment it reads the ledger until the
description and its ledger entry are both written, and then removes it.
A run that finds the lock refuses in plain words: "Another synthtwin
profile is running on this installation. Run again when it has
finished. If none is running (the computer stopped during a run),
delete <path> and run again." The ledger entry is written first, to a
temporary file moved into place with `os.replace`, and the description
after it, so two runs can never both find no entry and both publish
(Codex's item 9 of 2026-10-19), and a run stopped between the two
leaves an entry whose re-run, publishing the same description,
proceeds.

`--replace-description` is the person's declaration that the earlier
description of this table was never shared; the run then proceeds and
its entry replaces the table's earlier entry (name, key fingerprint and
digest). `--new-key` is accepted only where the ledger exists and no key
file can be read; it makes a new key and changes no ledger entry, so
every table described before stands under the old key's fingerprint
until a run with `--replace-description` replaces its entry. synthtwin
never replaces a key file that exists.

The content hash is the ledger's index and nothing else: it is never a
draw input and never published. A re-save that keeps every value gives
the same hash (a CSV and a workbook of one table included); a copy whose
values changed is a different table to the ledger, and so is a copy with
a column renamed, added or dropped, since the hash reads cells keyed by
column name (stated limit 2).

#### 4.6b.5 The chain and its tables (O2, O3)

**Amended 2026-10-21 (lane CHa, plan P4-D418): where the producer
publishes no chain.** `statistical` is also `null` (a) where a declared
person column repeats a value (`settings.person_columns` not empty), or
a column held by an open question offering `identifier`, or declared
an identifier, repeats one: the table may hold several rows per person,
which this section's proof does not cover (lane MG's page); nothing
waits, the description is written without a chain until the question
is answered; and (b) where a column's recount, cell by cell, disagrees
with its own published counts (the range bands against `K`, `missing`
against `n_missing`, a level against its count): the producer's own
check that 4.6b.2's obligations hold. Each publishes nothing between
columns, which the base product's description already is, so no proof
moves; the private notes say which.

**The tabled rows.** Every table of this section counts the TABLED ROWS:
every row of the table except the records holding nothing that a
published count places, `E` of them, the sum of
`source.dialect.empty_rows`' three counts on a text file or
`source.workbook.empty_rows_inside` on a workbook, a `null` read as
nought. A record holding nothing whose count is published as nought, or
withheld, stays a tabled row, so no table is a published count less a
cell (the held page's 4.6a.3, kept). Lane BTp's reservation (plan
P4-D404) reserves exactly `E` such records in the twin.

**`chain`** lists the families in chain order. Each entry is `{child,
level, parents, anchor, table, slopes}`:
- `child`, and `level` its CHAIN LEVEL (`L0`, `L1` or `L2`): the level
  of the family the column is the child of. A column stands at its chain
  level or coarser in every family that holds it (4.6b.3), so its chain
  level is the finest at which any table cuts it;
- `parents`: `[{column, level}]`, in schema order; empty for a family
  with no parent: the root pair's first column, at the level the root
  pair placed it, or a column placed by "no family", at `L0` (every
  column of a RULES-ONLY description, 4.6b.3);
- `anchor`: the index in `chain` of the earliest family holding every
  parent, or `null` where there is no parent;
- `table`: the family's COMPLETE count table over the tabled rows: one
  row for each joint cell of the parents at their levels (the parents in
  the order listed, each parent's bands in band order, the last parent's
  band varying fastest; one row where there is no parent), one column
  for each band of the child at its level in band order, every cell
  written, zeros included. Every cell is 0 or at least `f`, no cell is
  hidden, and a family that cannot meet the floor at any offered level
  is not placed (D3: merge bands, never hide a cell; the merging is the
  choice of a coarser level, 4.6b.3);
- `slopes`: 4.6b.6.

Every eligible column is the child of exactly one family. A family's
members are its child and its parents. The chain is a JUNCTION TREE in
the sense the proof uses (4.6b.9 (a)): each family's parents are members
of one earlier family, at levels no finer than that family holds them,
and each column's `L0` totals (4.6b.2) form a family of their own whose
one parent is the column's band at its chain level, a coarsening.

**Its size.** RULE W3 keeps a family's cells to at most `n / f`: each
member's bands each hold at least `f` times the product of the other
members' band counts, so `n` is at least `f` times the product of every
member's band count. The design's chain prototype (lane `A3`'s, under
its own floor and level rules, not under this section's RULE W3)
averaged 37 to 95 NON-ZERO cells a family over `k` = 1 to 3, at 17
columns and 20,000 rows (plan P4-D407). JUDGEMENT: 0.1 to 2 MB of text
at 200,000 rows.

**`procedure`** records the constants the profile ran under (4.6b.14),
so a loader checks a description against its own rules and a later
amendment moves no older description:
`{k_max, tau, w_rule, w_te, w_seed, uniform_share_bits, l0_cut, selftest_sample}`,
each weight a
fraction written as a string (`"1/20"`), `uniform_share_bits` 30 and
`l0_cut` naming the rungs `L0` uses (`deciles` in December).

**`rules`** lists each CARRIED rule (4.6b.7) once, in the order its step
was taken: `{kind, computed, inputs, carrier, class, derived}`. `kind`
is `order` or `formula` (lane MR adds the formula's arithmetic, which
this section does not fix); `computed` names the column the rule
computes (`B` of an order rule `A <= B`, or a formula's output);
`inputs` names its other columns in schema order; `carrier` is `null`,
or for an order rule the source column carrying its difference, or
`derived`; `class` is `"phrase"`, or the count of failing rows where
the carrier is `derived` (a source carrier and a formula rule take the
phrase only, 4.6b.7);
`derived` is `null` or the derived column's entry
`{name, edges, totals, parent, table}`: its one level's edges and band
totals, `parent` as `{column, level}` naming `A` and the level of `A`
its family holds, and
`table` the family `{D | A}`'s complete table laid out as a `chain`
table is. An inferred rule that is not carried is not listed.

#### 4.6b.6 Slopes (O4)

A family whose child is ORDERED and FINE may publish, for its ordered
fine parents together, one POOLED WITHIN-CELL SLOPE each and one
residual spread: `slopes` is `{parents: [{column, beta}], sigma}` or
`null`. They are read on each column's VALUE CODE (below): `beta` holds
the coefficients of the least-squares fit of the child's code on the
parents' codes inside the family's parent cells, the cells' own means
taken out (each cell its own intercept), pooled over every cell, and
`sigma` the root mean square of the fit's residuals. Each is written to
four decimals. The fit is solved in exact fractions by elimination in
the parents' order; a parent whose pivot is nought takes `beta` 0, and a
fit over rows whose parent codes do not vary inside any cell takes every
`beta` 0 (no division by nought; the held page's Codex item 4).

**A slope stands only where all of these hold** (the held page's
coefficient rule, kept for slopes):
1. at least 100 tabled rows hold a reading in the child and in every
   slope parent, counted on the family's published cells whose bands
   hold no spread cell, so the count is read from the description;
2. no side is a `binary` or label column;
3. every final band of each side that holds two or more different
   readings holds at least ten whose row counts the column's own
   published facts do not fix (a band holding one reading is exempt): a
   fact of one column, the producer's to keep and `K-S6-08`'s to check.

**FINE and the value code.** A column is FINE, taken as a whole, when it
holds more than 20 different readings and at least 10 readings whose
counts its own published facts do not fix (the moments' rule M1). A fine
column's VALUE CODE of a reading `x` is `min(255, max(0, floor(256 (x -
lo) / (hi - lo))))`, computed in exact fractions on the reading's own
value (a date's or a clock's ordinal), where `lo` and `hi` are the
outermost published rung pair whose tails each hold at least `f`
readings: `p01` and `p99` where the present readings number at least
1,100, else `p05` and `p95`, else `p10` and `p90` (M2); where `lo`
equals `hi` every code is 0. Lane MPOL's page uses the same code and
adds the second, rank-like code; this section uses only the first.

**What a slope's argument rests on.** A slope is one number read on
readings finer than the bands, a moment like the cell means of lane
MPOL's page. Whether one adds a small count beyond what that page's
integer witness covers is argued there (lane MPOL's page, item 4 of its
list in plan P4-D407) and checked by `K-S6-08`; it is not part of this
section's proof (4.6b.9 (h)). Whether a slope stands is decided on
published facts and on facts of one column (inventory row 27).

**AMENDED by ruling R12 (the orchestrator, 2026-10-20; lane MPOL's
page, plan P4-D413): where a slope is published.** A slope that stands
by the rule above is PUBLISHED only inside a PUBLISHING region of
section 4.6d (4.6d.3): its family is a node of that region and every
column it reads is a column of the region, so that Theorem 2 of 4.6d.5
covers it as condition (5) of every point of the region's joint space
(4.6d.4; 4.6d.5 (d) (i)). Anywhere else it is WITHHELD: the family's
`slopes` is `null`, as where no slope stands. So while the GATE of
4.6d.5 (h) is closed, `moments` is `null`, no region publishes and no
slope is published on any table; and on lane `A0b`'s chain, where under
`"cf1"` only `none` is eligible (4.6d.10, stated limit 3), none is.
*Reason:* the owner's ruling R10 (strict proof only, 2026-10-20): every
published number between columns needs a proof, and outside a
publishing region nothing proves that a slope adds no small count (this
page listed the slopes CHECKED, NOT PROVEN in 4.6b.9 (h)). *Price:* the
slopes withheld and the estimates they carried, UNMEASURED; lanes MPp
and CHa measure it on lane `E0b`'s battery (4.6d.10, stated limit 6).
Whether a slope STANDS is still decided by the rule above (inventory
row 27); this amendment decides only whether a slope that stands is
published, and every other clause of this section stands as written.

#### 4.6b.7 Rules between columns, computed columns and derived columns (with lane MR)

The rules the profiler infers between two columns (the owner's `D2r`
(a), as delegated: order rules such as admission before discharge, a
column a formula computes, a combination that never occurs) enter the
description in three ways only. Lane MR writes each rule kind's
inference and arithmetic, and its INFERENCE LIMIT (the largest count of
failing rows at which a rule is still inferred, at least `f`); this
section fixes what may be published about a rule and when.

**A rule is inferred only where its antecedent holds at least `f`
rows.** An inferred rule RAISES the weight of the chain's options that
hold its columns (4.6b.3); it never forces an edge. It is PUBLISHED only
as a rule word or as a carried rule, below. An inferred rule that is not
published is neither named nor enforced: its pair reads `implied` like
any pair outside a family (4.6b.8), and its failing rows are counted by
`K-BC-10` in the private report only. Naming it in the shared report
would publish what the draw masks: the second red team's P6 reads
"female and not pregnant" as exactly 8 with the rule named and as `[8,
20]` with the pair read `implied` (inventory row 7).

**RULE WORDS: a combination that never occurs is published only as a
zero of a placed family.** Every zero of a placed family's table (or of
a two-way margin of it: the child's band by one parent's band, or two
parents' bands) whose two bands each hold at least `f` rows over the
tabled rows is a RULE WORD, and nothing else is. A rule word is a
function of the published tables, so it is published by nothing but the
table that already shows it, and the generator meets it by meeting the
table (inventory row 8). A combination that occurs on 1 or more real
rows publishes no word: no phrase, no count, no enforcement.

**ORDER RULES and FORMULA RULES are CARRIED by a drawn step (inventory
rows 9, 9b, 10 and 14 of 4.6b.9 (b)).** An ORDER RULE `A <= B`, or a
FORMULA RULE (a column `C` equal to a formula of other columns, its
INPUTS, on every row but a few), is published only by a step of kind
`rule` of the draw (4.6b.4): one step for each inferred rule, all of
them taken before the chain is searched, in the schema order of the
column the rule would COMPUTE (`B` of an order rule, `C` of a formula
rule; ties by kind, `order` first, then by the inputs in schema order).
The step's options are "not carried", which is ALWAYS eligible, and the
CARRIED options below. "Not carried" scores 0, and a carried option
scores `w_rule n`, plus, where it places a family, that family's `u`
(4.6b.3). A rule whose computed column a rule carried before it computes
or reads as an input, or one of whose inputs a rule carried before it
computes, has "not carried" as its only option, so a column is computed
by at most one carried rule and no carried rule reads a computed
column.

*Its failing rows.* Each carried option has its own count `v` of
failing rows: for an order rule carried by a derived `D`, the rows where
both columns hold a reading and `B < A`; carried by a source column `D`,
those rows and the rows where `B` differs from `A + D` (a reading on one
side and none on the other included); for a formula rule, the rows where
`C` holds a reading and the formula gives another value or none (an
input absent), and the rows where every input holds a reading and `C`
holds none. Its PARTITION is the PHRASE "holds, except on at most
`f - 1` rows" ("at most 10 rows" at the default floor) for `v` from 0
to `f - 1`, the COUNT `v` itself for each `v` from `f` up to MR's
inference limit, and nothing above; the PHRASE-ONLY partition is the
phrase for `v` up to `f - 1` and nothing above. A derived carrier reads
the partition; a SOURCE carrier and a formula rule read the PHRASE-ONLY
partition alone. The twin writes the computed column from its rule on
every row, so it breaks a source-carried or formula rule on no row, and
a count class there would promise `v` failing rows that nothing places:
with twelve source rows where `B` is `A + D + 1`, writing `B` as `A + D`
leaves none of the twelve the class promised (Codex's item 3 of
2026-10-19). Only a derived carrier places its failing rows, as its
readings below 0 (the generation method's G16.2 step 5). A carried rule
publishes the class its real `v` falls in (`rules[].class`, 4.6b.5) and
nothing else of `v`.

*Its BASE.* The rule's base is the facts the description publishes
whether or not the rule is carried: the own facts (each column block,
and the `L0` totals of 4.6b.2) of the rule's columns that it does not
compute, that is `A`, and the source column `D` the inference names
where there is one, or a formula rule's inputs. It never holds the facts of the column the rule
would compute, since a carried rule withholds them (below), and it never
holds a family, since the chain is searched after every rule step. This
is the "description without the rule" of the design's row 9, read as the
facts the published description holds in either outcome: the first
review asked which description the test reads once publishing the rule
changes the column set, and only these facts are published both when
the rule is carried and when it is not.

*ROW 9's ONE TEST*, read once on the base and never on the real `v`.
The JOINT CELLS are the cells of the rule's base columns at their `L0`
bands, crossed with a mark, FAILS or HOLDS, read for the option being
tested: (`A`'s band, the named source `D`'s band where there is one, the
mark) for an order rule; (each input's band, the mark) for a formula
rule. A WORLD of a class `K` is a table of non-negative whole
numbers over the joint cells that agrees with every total the base
publishes about them and whose failing rows lie in `K`. A union of joint
cells LEAKS in `K` where its count lies inside 1 to `f - 1` in every
world of `K`. The test, in each class `K`: let `S(K)` be the joint cells
whose largest count over the worlds of `K` is at most `f - 1`; the class
PASSES where one world of `K` holds every cell of `S(K)` at 0. A
partition passes where each of its classes that publishes something
does. The joint cells read the base at its bands: a base column's own
facts finer than its bands (a source `D`'s count of negative readings, a
date's censuses) enter only through RULE W1 as own-fact groups, and
their crossing with the mark is a remainder (4.6b.9 (h)); lane MR's
measurement left the dates' censuses out in the same way.

- *Why a passing class leaks no union (proven).* Take a union `U` of
  joint cells. If `U` lies inside `S(K)`, the world that holds `S(K)` at
  0 holds `U` at 0. Otherwise `U` holds a cell whose largest count over
  `K` is at least `f`, so some world of `K` holds at least `f` rows in
  `U`. Either way `U`'s count is not inside 1 to `f - 1` in every world
  of `K`. ∎
- *It is computable.* Each largest count and each world is one exact
  integer program over the joint cells (the product of the base
  columns' `L0` band counts, twice; lane MR's fuller reading, which held
  the computed column's bands too, had 111 to 860 cells on its shapes),
  so the test never lists the unions. A class that does not pass is refused whether or not some
  union leaks there: the test may refuse more than it must, never pass a
  leak.
- *The implementation route* (the orchestrator's ruling of 2026-10-19,
  14:11, on lane MR's measurement): an exact integer solver, scipy's
  HiGHS, decided row 9 in 0.01 to 7.5 seconds a rule on the design's
  emergency, lab and stay shapes; lanes MR and CHa take it, subject to
  lane DEP's offline bundle (plan P4-D407). Every world a solver returns
  is re-checked in whole-number arithmetic.

A CARRIED option is ELIGIBLE where RULE WE holds with it placed
(4.6b.3), the partition passes the test, the
real `v` lies in one of its classes, and the base forces the rule's
ANTECEDENT (the rows where every base column, and for a derived `D` the
difference, holds a reading) to at least `f` rows: for a derived `D` its
value bands (rule 1 below); otherwise the base columns' present rows
summed, less the tabled rows times one fewer than their number. Where
the partition does not pass but the phrase-only partition does, the
phrase-only partition is read the same way; where neither passes, only
"not carried" is eligible. Lane MR's inference opens a rule's step on
the real table, and owes that every table a carried rule's description
allows opens the same step: its conditions are to be implied by the
base, the class and the antecedent bound (Lemma 2, 4.6b.9 (b)). That is
a PRECONDITION of the proof for inventory rows 9, 9b, 10 and 14, OPEN
until lane MR's page proves it: those rows are proven on that condition
only (4.6b.9 (h)).
Which partition applies is a function of the base, which the description
publishes whenever the rule is carried, and the class is published with
the rule, so a carried option's eligibility is a function of the
description it is placed in, and "not carried" is open on every table.
A refused or undrawn rule leaves its pair `implied` and its failing rows
broken on about half the twin's rows (below).

**What a carried order rule publishes.** An order rule `A <= B` is
carried by its DIFFERENCE `D = B - A`, in one of two kinds of option,
both offered by the rule's step where eligible: by a SOURCE column `D`
that lane MR's inference names (a column equal to `B - A` on most rows;
the option's failing rows then count the rows where `B` differs from
`A + D` as well, so the identity is held to the same partition and the
same test as the order; inventory row 10), or by a DERIVED `D` (below).
A source `D` is offered only where its own block publishes `n_negative`
0: the twin keeps `D`'s cells, so six negative readings of `D` beside a
present `A` would break the order on six twin rows, which the phrase
promises it does not (Codex's item 3 of 2026-10-19).
`B` is COMPUTED: in every row of the twin it is written as `A + D`,
where both hold a reading, and absent elsewhere, so `B >= A` on every
row where `D >= 0`; it is written in `A`'s published layout words (the
generation method's G16.2 step 5), since `B` publishes none of its own
(below). Where a source `D` carries the rule, the weight raise goes to
the chain's option `{D | A}`. MR's page writes a formula rule's
arithmetic and the layout of its output. In the phrase class the twin
breaks the rule on no row; in a count class, which only a derived
carrier takes, on exactly `v` rows, its readings below 0.

**What a computed column publishes: its name, its place and its role,
and nothing read from its cells.** A column a carried rule computes
publishes no count, statistic, form or word of its cells, so no exact
cumulative count of it exists (inventory row 9 and the third attack's
B3) and no fact of its cells tells its failing rows from none. THE RULE:
its block keeps `name`, `position` and `role`, and writes EVERY other
key `null`, or `{}` where the key holds an object and `[]` where it
holds a list: every universal key of section 5.1 that counts its cells
or describes them in words (`n_present`, `n_missing`,
`missing_by_class`, `missing_by_source`, `n_missing_blank`,
`n_missing_withheld`, `n_distinct`, `n_distinct_folded`, `n_numeric`,
`n_not_numeric`, `n_out_of_range`, `n_contradictory`,
`n_sentinel_candidates_unpublished`, `sentinel_verdicts`,
`statistical_type`, `quality_state`, `structural_role`,
`detection_evidence`, `remarks`), and every key the matrix of section
6.11 lists for its role, whether it holds a count, a share, a rung, a
moment, a census, a heap, a tail, a histogram, a width, a form or a
word. The keys a reader could otherwise subtract are named so that no
reading of the rule leaves them: for numbers `numeric_styles`,
`fraction_widths`, `pad_widths`, `field_widths`, `number_spellings`,
`n_zero`, `n_negative`, `mean`, `std`, `skew`, `mode`, `mode_count`,
`percentiles`, `percentiles_between` and `value_histogram`; for dates and
clocks `n_unparsed`, `datetime_separators`, `utc_offsets`, `zulu_case`,
`quarter_marker_case`, `month_name_styles`, `date_field_widths`,
`resolution_mix`, `heavy_dates` and the calendar censuses; the counts
of `shape_forms` and `layout_forms` wherever its role lists them; and `integer_valued`,
a format and a resolution, each read from its cells. Its `L0` totals,
any ladder and any family are withheld too. Why the census goes: `B`'s
`numeric_styles` `{"integer": 980}` less `D`'s present rows (978, 975
and 971) fixed "`A` absent, `B` recorded" at 2, 5 and 9 on the first
review's 1,000 rows (the verify of 2026-10-19, item 1, MEASURED; a
timestamp `B`'s `datetime_separators` gives the same, and `B`'s `n_zero`
beside `A`'s fixes "`A` = 0 and `D` = 0"). Why the words go: with `A`
and a source `D` publishing `integer_valued` true, `B`'s `false` would
say that some row holds `B` other than `A + D`, a failing row, so the
phrase "at most `f - 1`" would read 1 to `f - 1`. The twin writes the
column in its rule's layout (an order rule's `B` in `A`'s published
layout words; a formula's output as lane MR's page fixes), a move of a
computed column's written forms that `K-S6-02` lists and the private
report names. The landing that ships stage 6 amends section 5.1 and the
role sections to allow `null`, `{}` and `[]` there on a column
`ineligible` as `computed`, and nowhere else, and waives on it every
invariant that reads a withheld key, among them P1 and P3
(`numeric_styles`), D13 (`datetime_separators`), SF3 (`shape_forms`),
and LF3 and LF4 (`layout_forms`). `synthtwin validate` prints none of
its counts (validation method `V12.3`). Its absent cells are withheld
with the rest: with `A`'s absent cells and `D`'s present rows
published, the count of `B`'s absent cells would fix the rows where `A`
is absent and `B` holds a reading (the first review measured 2 and 5
such rows on 1,000 rows). Every count a reader can form about a computed column is a
count over `(A, D)`: at band level a union of floored family cells (the
theorem, 4.6b.9 (a)); finer than the bands, `A`'s and `D`'s own facts
read together across two columns, which is the design's straddle count,
checked and not proven (4.6b.9 (d)).

**A DERIVED column** `D`, made because the source has no column equal to
`B - A`, exists only inside its rule's entry of `rules`: it is not a
candidate, has no `ladder` entry and stands in no family of `chain`
(4.6b.1). It is published ONLY as the child of one family `{D | A}`,
placed by the rule's own step: each carried option of that step is one
pair (a LEVEL of `D`, a level of `A`), and its family's table is counted
over the tabled rows. `D`'s levels are its own nested cuts, computed
from its readings by the contract's interpolation rule: the deciles with
`p25` and `p75`, then `p25`, `p50`, `p75` and `p90`, then `p50`, then
one value band, each with tied edges taken once; beside its value bands
every level holds `D`'s `missing` band, the rows where `A` or `B` holds
no reading. `A` stands at any of its three levels. The option is
ELIGIBLE where:
1. every value band of `D` holds at least `max(2 f, f + 4)` rows (this
   reads `D`'s value bands only, never its `missing` band or the tabled
   rows, which the first draft's "fewer than `max(2 f, f + 4)` tabled
   rows" confused);
2. `A`'s `missing` band is a band of its own (its `L0` total 0 or at
   least `f`, never merged with a neighbour), so the family's row for
   `A` absent holds every such row in `D`'s `missing` band and 0 in every
   value band: the STRUCTURAL ZEROS of a derived column, published as
   cells of its table;
3. every cell of the family's table is 0 or at least `f`, so the rows
   where `A` holds a reading and `B` does not are, in each band of `A`,
   0 or at least `f`;
4. RULE W1 (4.6b.3) holds with the family placed, `D`'s one level read
   as its coarsest;
5. in a COUNT class, cutting `D`'s level at 0 (the band holding 0 split
   into its readings below 0 and the rest) leaves every band 0 or at
   least `f`; in the phrase class this always holds (4.6b.9 (e)).

The carried option publishes `D`'s level (its edges and totals), the
family's table and the rule's class, and no other count of `D`: no
`n_zero`, `n_negative`, `mode_count`, heap, tail rows, bin groups, field
widths or any other one-value count; the acceptance of facts of one
column (plan P4-D363) covers SOURCE columns only (the third attack's
B4). Where no pair of levels is eligible, only "not carried" is. Why
the family, the structural zeros and the class leave no count of 1 to
`f - 1` to work out, and why an interpolated edge bounds none: 4.6b.9
(e). The first review's case shows what the family closes: with `D`'s
band totals published alone at one level (the first draft), `A`'s absent
cells and `D`'s present rows fixed the rows "admission recorded,
discharge absent" at 14, 10 or 7 on 1,000 rows; under rule 3 those rows
are a sum of family cells each 0 or at least `f`, and where they number
1 to `f - 1` no option is eligible.

**The price** (the orchestrator's addendum of 2026-10-19, 14:11, on
lane MR's measurement; plan P4-D407). A rule that is not carried leaves
its pair `implied`, and the twin breaks it on about half its rows: 49.8
per cent of 20,000 twin rows broke "discharge on or after admission"
when an order rule was refused (MEASURED by lane MR; `K-BC-10`, named in
the private report). Lane MR measured the test reading the design's
literal "description without the rule", which holds the computed
column's own band totals: there a batch of keying errors larger than the
rows crossing one rung forwards (5, 8 and 87 rows at 20,000 rows on the
emergency, lab and stay shapes) refuses the rule, because those totals
force 1 to `f - 1` failing rows. The base above withholds those totals
(a carried rule publishes none of them), so they force nothing and such
a batch is no refusal under this section; the price here is a derived
`D` whose family fails rule 2 or 3 at every pair of levels, which lane
MR prices on the same shapes before lane CHa builds the step.

#### 4.6b.8 Words (O7), names (O8), the two reports, and the content hash

**`words`: one STRUCTURAL WORD a candidate pair**, a function of the
description alone (inventory row 30): `exact` where the two columns are
members of one placed family; `pinned` where they are not and lane
MPOL's object publishes a correlation between them (RESERVED: no pair
reads `pinned` before that page lands); `implied` otherwise. `words`
lists every candidate pair once, in schema order, as `{columns, word}`.

**`not_carried`** lists the pairs reading `implied`, with NO reason:
which rule or draw left a pair out is never published (inventory rows 4
and 34). **`ineligible`** lists each ineligible column once, `{column,
reason}`, with 4.6b.1's reasons only. **`withheld`** is RESERVED for
lane MPOL: a column or pair and ONE moment-class word (`mean`, `spread`,
`correlation`, `product`), never the rule that withheld it; it is empty
in a description of this layer alone.

**The analysis families' grades** are constants of this version, written
in the twin's report, not in the description: `E` (exact at the
published bands) for rates, cross-tables and logistic models on banded
predictors inside one family; `P` (pinned on the code scale) where lane
MPOL's moments stand; `A` (approximate: as the chain implies) elsewhere;
`N` where neither column of a pair takes part. By analysis family: rates
and cross-tables, `E` inside a family at its bands and `A` across
families; correlations and least squares among fine columns, `P` on the
code scale where lane MPOL's moments stand and `A` on a skewed column's
log or raw scale; logistic models, `E` on banded predictors in the
outcome's family and `A` otherwise; survival models, `A`; several rows
per patient, lane MG's; trees and boosting, `A`; missing data by other
columns, `E` inside a family and `A` otherwise; code run unchanged, `E`
within columns; three or more columns together, `E` inside a family and
`N` otherwise.

**A grade `E` is owed only where the twin met the family's published
table.** Where this twin's family was made against a MOVED target (the
generation method's G16.6: a member made without its published band
totals, or parent cells an earlier move changed), the twin does not
hold the published table: the twin's report grades that family's pairs
and analyses `A`, and names the family "moved in this twin" beside its
structural word, which stays the description's (Codex's item 14 of
2026-10-19: the move from `[[50, 0], [0, 50]]` to `[[40, 20], [0, 40]]`
changes the family's rates and adds a combination the real table never
held). Whether a family was moved is a function of the description and
the seed.

**The two reports (the owner's answer to question 12, 2026-10-18, ruling
R7 (2)).**
- **The SHARED report** is the twin's report, written by `generate` and
  travelling with the twin. Its between-columns lines print structural
  grades only: each pair's word, each analysis family's grade, and
  example lines in that vocabulary ("Logistic models for died: exact for
  age band and admission type, which share its family; implied for crp"). It prints
  no real estimate, no rate, no gap and no reason a pair was left out,
  and it says, in one line, that each table should be described once, on
  one installation, under one name, with the same columns under the same
  names, a copy with a column renamed, added or dropped being described
  as another table (4.6b.13).
- **The twin's DEVIATIONS**, a section of the same report that every
  twin's report carries today (the generation method's named
  deviations), list what this twin did not meet of its description,
  each a function of the description and the seed alone, which anyone
  holding both recomputes by generating the twin again: they print no
  fact of the real table. For this layer they name each family made
  against a moved target, with the cells the move changed and the units
  it placed in a published nought, and each stray row left (the
  generation method's G16.5). They are no grade: R7 (2) restricts the
  grades the shared report prints, and gate clause (3)'s "no published
  or achieved value" is said of the pair lines, while a deviation counts
  the twin's own rows, never the real table's (Codex's item 13 of
  2026-10-19 asked which surface prints them).
- **The PRIVATE report** is written in the private output folder of the
  person who ran `synthtwin profile` on their own table, and is never
  part of the description, the twin, a log or the shared report. It
  carries, for every pair and every analysis family, BOTH the structural
  grade and the self-check's JUDGED grade (lane ST's self-test, judged
  at the whole table's precision), says plainly which of the two to act
  on (the judged grade, which was measured on this table; the structural
  grade is what the people the twin is shared with see), and ADVISES
  which twin to use for which analyses: where the twin's numbers can
  stand in for the real table's (an `exact` or `pinned` pair, an
  analysis judged carried), and where the twin is for developing code
  only, which is then run unchanged on the real table (an `implied`
  pair, an analysis judged approximate or not carried). It names why a
  family was not placed or a rule not published, the rows each rule
  fails on (`K-BC-10`), and the key file's path, never the key. Lanes ST
  and TT build it; the owner's words are R7 (2).

**The CONTENT HASH of a row** is BLAKE2b (`hashlib.blake2b`, unkeyed,
`digest_size=32`, `person=b"synthtwin.row.1"`) over the row's cells as
the reader parsed them, taken in the order of their column names, each
written as the column name's UTF-8 bytes and then the cell's text's
UTF-8 bytes (a cell read as holding nothing is the empty text), each of
the two preceded by its own length in bytes as 8 bytes big-endian: a
LENGTH-FRAMED encoding, which no text can imitate. The first build's
separator bytes `0x1f` and `0x1e` could stand inside a cell, so under
columns `A` and `B` the rows `("x\u001eB\u001fy", "z")` and `("x",
"y\u001eB\u001fz")` wrote the same bytes and took one hash with no
collision of BLAKE2b (Codex's item 15 of 2026-10-19). **The table's content hash** is
the sum of its rows' content hashes, each read as a big-endian whole
number, modulo `2**256`: free of row order, of column order and of the
file's form, since it reads parsed cells keyed by column name (lane CHa
specifies "parsed" for each form, with a test that a CSV and a workbook
of one table give one hash). It is used only as the ledger's index
(4.6b.4). **Amended 2026-10-21 (lane CHa's repair 1, plan P4-D418):** a
row whose cells all hold nothing is left out of the table's content
hash, so a table with one more empty record is the same table to the ledger,
which refuses it under a second name; measured by lane CHa's skeptic,
`clinic.csv` with one line of empty cells added had proceeded under a
new name with no refusal and published a different chain.

**The self-test's sample** (layer `L2b`, lane ST) is chosen by content and
SORTED by content before anything is generated from it, so a whole-row
shuffle of the real table changes nothing (the held page's Codex item
14). Each row's SAMPLE KEY is BLAKE2b (`digest_size=8`,
`person=b"synthtwin.smp.1"`) over its content hash followed by its
OCCURRENCE, the count of earlier rows with the same content hash,
written as 8 bytes big-endian: equal rows are interchangeable, so the
multiset of keys is a function of the content alone, and each copy of
a repeated row takes a key of its own. The sample is the `min(m, n)`
rows of smallest key, `n` the tabled rows and `m` the constant
`selftest_sample` of 4.6b.14 (in December 20,000 below 1,000,000
tabled rows and 200,000 from there), equal keys (a chance of `2**-64`)
taken in order of content hash and then occurrence; it is sorted by
key. It holds exactly `min(m, n)` rows: none only where the table has
no tabled row, and never more. The
first build sampled a row where the first 8 bytes of its content hash
fell below a cut, which took or left every copy of a row together: on
500,000 rows `0,0` beside 500,000 rows `1,1` it took no row, and on
other tables with many equal rows half the table or no row of one
category (Codex's item 8 of 2026-10-19); keyed by occurrence, that
table gives about 100,000 rows of each. Counting occurrences holds one
count for each different row while the sample is drawn; lane ST
measures it under the 2.5 GB watchdog. Its simulation's words are SplitMix64
outputs keyed by a constant and by the sampled rows' hashes (lane ST
writes them). The triple screen's seeds (4.6b.3) read the same sample.
No content hash is ever a draw input of RULE W5 (R6).

#### 4.6b.9 Why no small count can be worked out: the proofs

Each argument below states what it proves, the reader it proves it for,
and its own remainder, CHECKED, NOT PROVEN, which `K-S6-08`'s
enumeration checks (4.6b.10). The enumeration is the check of each
argument, never its substitute.

**(a) The table theorem (one row per patient).**

*Setting.* `n` is the tabled rows (4.6b.5). The FULL JOINT TABLE gives,
for each combination `x` of one `L0` band of every eligible column (a
CELL), the number of rows holding it. `Omega(D)` is every table of
non-negative whole numbers over those cells, summing to `n`, whose sums
agree with every family table of `D` (each family's members at its
levels; a band of a coarser level is the union of the `L0` bands inside
it) and with every column's `L0` totals. A UNION is any set of cells.
`b(x)`, the CELL BOUND, is the smallest published number counting a set
of rows that holds `x`: every family cell whose bands hold `x`'s bands,
every `L0` total of `x`'s bands, and `n`. Every such number is 0 or at
least `f`: family cells by the floor (4.6b.3), `L0` totals by the merge
(4.6b.2). (A table of fewer than `f` tabled rows has no eligible column,
since its `L0` merge leaves every column one band, and publishes no
chain.) A DERIVED column (4.6b.7) counts here as one more column, its
`L0` bands being its one level's bands (cut at 0 in a count class), and
its family `{D | A}` as one more published table; its bands' totals and
cells are 0 or at least `f` by the rules that made it eligible.

*Lemma 1 (the cell bound is sharp and attained by whole numbers).* For
every cell `x`, every table of `Omega(D)` holds at most `b(x)` rows in
`x`, and one table of `Omega(D)` holds exactly `b(x)`.

*Proof.* The first half: each number `b(x)` is read from is a sum of
cells including `x`, all non-negative. The second half builds a table
`T*` family by family in chain order, as the generator's walk does
(G16.2), keeping two things true after each family: the table built so
far agrees with every family placed so far, and it holds in `x`'s cell
(read at the columns placed so far) the smallest of the published cells
of those families that hold `x`. Take the next family `F`, child `d`,
parents `P` at their levels, anchor `A`. Its parents are members of `A`,
already placed, and `F`'s table summed over `d` equals `A`'s table
summed to `P` at `F`'s levels (invariant S25). So inside each joint cell
`pi` of the parents, the rows the table so far holds are split over the
cells `y` of the columns placed so far that lie in `pi`, with totals
`t(y)`, and those totals sum to `N(pi)`, the row total of `F`'s table at
`pi`. Dealing `d`'s bands to those rows is filling a two-way table, `y`
by `d`'s band, with row totals `t(y)` and column totals `F(pi, delta)`,
both summing to `N(pi)`; such a whole-number table always exists, and
the north-west corner rule with `x`'s own `y*` and `delta*` taken first
puts `min(t(y*), F(pi*, delta*))` into their cell. Both properties then
hold for `F`. A family with no parent is the same step with one `pi`.
Last, each column's `L0` totals are a family whose one parent is the
column's own band at its chain level, and the same step splits each
chain-level band into its `L0` bands; after them each derived family
`{D | A}`, whose parent `A` stands at a level that is a union of `A`'s
`L0` bands, is dealt by the same step, and in a count class the split of
`D`'s band at 0 after it. `T*` agrees with every published table and
holds `b(x)` in `x`. ∎ (The bound for a decomposable set of
margins is Dobra and Fienberg's, PNAS 97(22), 2000; the construction
above is self-contained.)

*Theorem 1.* For every union `U`, either every table of `Omega(D)` holds
0 rows in `U`, or some table of `Omega(D)` holds at least `f` rows in
`U`. So no count of rows in a union is fixed at, or bounded inside, 1 to
`f - 1` by the published tables.

*Proof.* If some cell `x` of `U` has `b(x)` above 0, then `b(x)` is at
least `f`, and the table of Lemma 1 for `x` holds at least `f` rows in
`U`. Otherwise every cell of `U` has `b(x)` = 0, and by Lemma 1's first
half every table holds 0 there. ∎

*What it covers.* A single family cell; any sum or difference of
published cells (each is a union); two tables sharing a column, whose
margins are equal (S25), so their difference is nought on every band; a
column cut at two levels in two tables, whose bands nest, so no two of
its cuts cross (the linked-table leak needs cuts that do not nest, and
none do); STRUCTURAL ZEROS and RULE WORDS, which are published cells
holding 0, so a union inside them holds 0 in every table (and 0 may be
printed); and every combination of the whole published set of tables at
once. MEASURED by the design's chain prototype (plan P4-D407): 0 counts
of 1 to 10 fixed or bounded among 196,608,000 unions over 3,000 random
tables, against 3,316 counts on 2,139 of 24,493 tables when every pair's
table is published instead, which is why every pair's table is not
(three of the design's candidates measured such loops independently).

*What it does not cover, and who does.* A count finer than the `L0`
bands: a column's own facts (RULE W1, (c) below), the slopes (4.6b.6)
and the moments (lane MPOL), and a table with several rows per patient,
where a cell of `f` rows can be fewer than `f` people (lane MG). Each is
named with its owner in (h).

**(b) The draw lemma: the procedure's reader is told no more than the
numbers say.**

A reader who knows this section's procedure, but not the key, can
exclude every table from which the procedure would have published
something else. *The model.* The words of RULE W5 are read as
independent choices with the chances 4.6b.4 gives them: a reader without
the key cannot tell keyed BLAKE2b words from such choices (the
pseudorandom property of keyed BLAKE2b, ASSUMED, not proven here). R3's
"no key-unknown draw could have published `D`" is read in that model:
what counts is the chance a draw gives, never a search of the key's
`2**256` values, which is beyond any reader's computation (an assumption
of the same kind) and which a reader who holds the key has no need of
(stated limit 2).

*Lemma 2.* Let `CONS(D)` be every table, with its readings, whose every
published fact equals `D`'s. If every decision the procedure takes from
the real table is either (a) drawn by W5 among options whose
eligibility, for a placed option, is a function of `D`, with every
eligible option given a chance above nought, or (b) itself a function of
facts `D` publishes, then the preimage of `D` is `CONS(D)`.

*Proof.* The preimage lies inside `CONS(D)` by definition. Take a table
`T` of `CONS(D)` and run the procedure on it. Each decision of class (b)
reads facts `D` publishes, which `T` shares, so it decides as it did on
the real table. Each rule step `D` carries opens on `T` too (lane MR's
obligation, 4.6b.7: a PRECONDITION of this proof for rows 9, 9b, 10 and
14, open until MR's page proves it), and a rule step `T` opens that `D` does not list
can draw "not carried", which is always eligible. At each drawn step
the offered options are the same (row 3 below is (b)), in the same
option order, and the option `D` placed is eligible on `T`, since its
eligibility reads only `D` (its table, which `T` shares, and published
facts); "no family" and "not carried" are always eligible. So the
placed option has a chance of at least `2**-30` times `floor(2**64 /
m_T) / 2**64` on `T`, `m_T` being `T`'s count of eligible options; the
steps' words are independent, since their inputs differ (4.6b.4); so the
chance that every step of the run on `T` places what `D` places is the
product of numbers above nought. The numbers then published are `T`'s
counts at the placed levels, which are `D`'s. So `T` is in the preimage.
∎

*Corollary (the procedure's reader).* `Omega(D)` holds exactly the full
joint tables of `CONS(D)` (each column's readings can be dealt to the
rows of its `L0` bands in any order, since in the table layer without
slopes and moments no published fact reads which row holds which reading
inside a band; the facts that read positions, the sort, the records
holding nothing and blank lines, are kept by placing whole rows, as the
twin does), so Theorem 1 holds over the preimage: tables, levels,
placements, anchors, rule words and structural words tell a reader who
knows the procedure exactly what they tell a reader of the numbers.
One published fact reads across every column at once: the census of
records holding nothing, which leaves at most `Z` tabled rows blank in
every column (4.6b.3, RULE WE). Under RULE WE every table of `Omega(D)`
holds at most `b(x0)`, so at most `Z + P`, rows blank in every eligible
column; the columns outside the ladder stand in no family, so their
non-blank cells can be dealt to any rows, those first, and the rest
are records holding nothing of the counts published as nought. So
every table of `Omega(D)` extends to a table of `CONS(D)`, and the
census removes none (Codex's item 1 of 2026-10-19 showed that without
the rule it can: its 133-row case fixes a count at 6). A
derived column's readings are dealt inside its bands likewise, and a
table of `Omega(D)` builds a real one (`B` written as `A + D` where `D`
holds a reading, absent where `A` does and `D` does not, and free where
`A` is absent, since a computed `B` publishes nothing read from its
cells but its role, 4.6b.7). That needs the
STRUCTURAL ZEROS of 4.6b.7 rule 2 to be published cells, so that
`Omega(D)` holds no table in which `D` holds a reading beside an absent
`A`: the first draft published `D`'s band totals alone, its `Omega(D)`
held such tables, and the first review read a count across columns off
the difference (4.6b.7).

*Full support in binary64.* A weight can be `0.0` (the stated
exponential of a gap of 5,000 at `tau` = 2 underflows), so the weighted
choice alone would not give every eligible option a chance; the uniform
share does, at `2**-30` divided by the option count, exactly, whatever
the weights. The option count at a step is far below `2**64`, so `(U2 *
m) >> 64` reaches every option.

*The inventory: every decision the profiler takes from the real table*
(the design's inventory as its three repairs left it; the lemma holds
once every row is (a) or (b)). Rows owned by another page are listed
with their owner and are that page's to prove; this section's proof
covers the rows marked MBC.

| # | decision | class here, and why | proves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | the root pair; each step's placed option or "no family" | (a): drawn (4.6b.4) | MBC |
| 1a | a family's anchor | (b): the earliest family in chain order holding every parent, a function of the published chain | MBC |
| 2 | a placed family's level variant | (a): every variant is a separate option of the same draw | MBC |

*Every count, for the rows of this layer (ruling R8 (2)).* The lemma's
clause (b) asks that a decision published as a word or class leave EVERY
count 0-able or at least `f` in each outcome's preimage, not the one
count a fixture tests. For rows 1a, 3, 8, 11 (its detection), 27
(whether a slope stands), 28, 30 and 34 the outcome is a function of the
rest of the description, so it removes no table from the preimage: every
count keeps the range Theorem 1 gives it. Rows 9, 9b, 10 and 14 are now
drawn (class (a)): "not carried" is open on every table, so that outcome
removes no table either. A carried rule's outcome is its published
class; its preimage is the tables the rest of the description allows
whose failing rows lie in that class, and:
- over the BASE, the one test's sufficient form (4.6b.7, proven there)
  leaves every union of the joint cells 0-able or reaching `f` in that
  class: every union, not only unions of three cells, and computed
  exactly, never sampled;
- for an order rule carried by a DERIVED `D`, (e) below proves the class
  beside the whole description: every count over the full joint table,
  `D`'s bands and its failing rows included;
- for an order rule carried by a SOURCE column, and for a formula rule,
  a union reading the failing rows together with a family of the chain
  is cut only through the readings of the rule's columns inside their
  bands. The walk deals the columns outside the families holding the
  rule's columns independently of those readings given their separators,
  so such a union keeps its range: JUDGEMENT, CHECKED by `K-S6-08` on the
  fixtures of 4.6b.10 (lane MR's emergency, lab and stay shapes with the
  family `{B | A}` placed read 0 leaking unions over 256 outcome
  classes), not proven.

The patient layer's rows (15a, 16, 18b, 19) are lane MG's to argue.

**(c) RULE W1: a column's own small groups beside the tables.**

The theorem is about bands. A column's own facts can fix the count of a
group FINER than a band, an OWN-FACT GROUP `G` of `g` rows (4.6b.3).
Published zeros can confine every row of the band `beta` holding `G` to
one band of another column `m`; the count "`G` AND that band" is then
`g`, a count across two columns fixed inside 1 to `f - 1` (the red
team's part C: `n_zero` 6 inside a band of 25 rows reading post-op
(25, 0) fixed "day 0 AND post-op 0" at 6).

*Setting.* The description of this layer without slopes and moments
(with them the readings inside a band are no longer free, and lane
MPOL's joint-space witness takes over: (h)). `beta0` is the `L0` band of
`c` holding `G` and `beta` the band of `c`'s chain level holding
`beta0`. `S(beta0)`, the SUPPORT, is the cells `x` of the full joint
table with `c` in `beta0` and `b(x)` above 0. Since `c`'s `L0` bands are
a family whose one parent is `c`'s chain-level band (4.6b.5), the
support's cells differ from those beside `beta` only in `c`'s own
coordinate, so W1, which reads `beta`, reads `S(beta0)`.

*Lemma 3.* Under RULE W1, for every union `U` of cells of the full joint
table, the count of `G`'s rows in `U` over the preimage either (i) has 0
in its range, or reaches `f` when `g` does; or (ii) `U` holds every cell
of `S(beta0)`, and then `G`'s rows in `U` are `G` itself in every table
of the preimage. And for every other eligible column `m` and every band
`delta` of every published level of `m`, "`G` AND `m` in `delta`" has 0
in its range unless `delta` holds every band of `m` that the support
admits; at `m`'s coarsest level no band does.

*Proof.* Exchanging `c`'s readings between two rows of `beta0` keeps
every band of every column, every family table, every `L0` total and
`c`'s multiset of readings (a sort by `c` is kept by moving whole rows
after it), so it maps a table of `CONS(D)` to a table of `CONS(D)`,
which is the preimage (Lemma 2). If `U` misses a cell `x` of `S(beta0)`,
then `b(x)` is at least `f`; take Lemma 1's table for `x`, which holds
at least `f` rows in `x`, and exchange `G`'s readings onto rows of `x`:
where `g` is below `f`, `G` then holds 0 rows in `U`. Where `g` is `f`
or more and `U` holds a cell `x'` of the support, Lemma 1's table for
`x'` and the same exchange put `min(g, b(x'))`, at least `f`, of `G`'s
rows in `U`; a union holding no cell of the support holds none of `G`'s
rows in any table. That is (i). If `U` holds every cell of `S(beta0)`,
every row of `beta0` lies in `U` in every table of the preimage (a cell
outside the support holds no row in any, by Lemma 1), and `G` lies in
`beta0`: that is (ii). The last sentence: W1 makes the support admit two
bands of `m`'s `L2`, so for any band `delta` of `m` at any level, some
cell of the support has `m` outside `delta` (a band of `L0` or `L1` lies
inside one band of `L2`), and the first case applies. ∎

*Corollaries.* "`G` AND a family cell" ranges over `[0, g]` (the
design's statement). Two groups of one band, or of several bands of one
column, add band by band. A group `G` of `c` beside a group `H` of `m`:
"`G` AND `H`" has 0 in its range, since `G` can be exchanged onto a cell
of its support whose `m` band at `L2` does not hold `H`'s band. Several
families holding `c`, and columns of other families, are covered because
the support is read over the whole chain.

*Case (ii) is a READING of R1, confirmed by the orchestrator's ruling of
2026-10-19 (12:14) on this page's first build (plan P4-D407).* In case
(ii) the count is `G`'s own count: the union holds every combination
the published tables admit beside `beta0`, so `G`'s rows lie in it in
every table of the preimage, and the count equals, in every world, a
fact the column already publishes about itself. Such a count adds no
exposure (R3 reads a leak over the preimage, and plan P4-D363 accepts a
column's own facts within one column), PROVIDED that RULE W1 fixes no
band of any published level of any other column for `G`, which the last
sentence of Lemma 3 gives. Read otherwise, R1 would forbid any small
own-fact group beside any published zero of any table, including zeros
between columns `G`'s column never meets.

What the reading accepts, stated so the owner's reviewers can weigh it
(the first review's construction, MY ARITHMETIC): 1,000 rows; a days
column with `n_zero` 6 inside an `L0` band of 100 rows; an admission
type with levels A 280, B 240, C 240 and D 240 rows, its `L2` being A
against the rest; the family row of that band reading A 56, B 0, C 44,
D 0. W1 passes (A and C lie in two `L2` bands of the type), and "days 0
AND type A or C" is 6 in every table: the union {A, C} is every
combination the tables admit beside the band. A reader is told that the
six rows with days 0 have type A or C, a set of levels that is no band
of any published level of the type. Why that differs from part C's
single band: there the union was a band of another column's published
level, so a published category of that column was fixed for `G`, which
W1 forbids; here only the combinations the band's own published cells
already allow are named. The case is a `K-S6-08` fixture, reported as
accepted under the ruling and never as a pass (4.6b.10), and stated
limit 3 of 4.6b.13 names it.

*Why W1 is read at the coarsest level, member by member and across the
chain.* The design's own clause, "the row of `beta` in the option's table
holds at least two non-zero cells", lets three cases through, each a
count of the part-C kind: (1) a parent cut at `L0` whose two non-zero
cells beside `beta` both lie below its median: "`G` AND the parent below
its median" is `g`, since `L2`'s band is a published union; (2) a family
of two parents whose two non-zero cells beside `beta` share one parent's
band; (3) a band of `c` whose admitted cells in its own family lead,
through a zero of another family, to one band of a column outside `c`'s
families. This section's reading refuses all three (MY ARITHMETIC on
Lemma 3; no probe has measured how often they occur). The price is fine
levels refused where a band of a column with own-fact groups is confined
in another column; the coarser variant or "no family" is drawn instead.
Lanes `A0b` and CHa count the refusals on the zoo, as the design asked its
bake-off to count W1's. MEASURED on the part-C example by the design's
probe (plan P4-D407): with W1 as a filter, "day 0 AND post-op 0" ranges
over `[0, 6]` and 0 of 1,030 descriptions leak, against a fixed 6 and
423 of 1,453 with the merge W1 replaced; the example has one parent, so
this section's reading decides it the same way.

*W1 is checked in full at every step* (4.6b.3). The first build checked
only the pairs holding the step's child, on the claim that adding a
family never narrows an earlier support; the claim fails where the
step's child already stands in a placed family. Codex's case (item 2 of
2026-10-19), on 100 rows: `C` holds 6 absent cells, 44 `u` and 50 `v`,
its `L0` merge joining the six with `u` into a band of 50 (the six an
own-fact group); `E` has two levels of 50; `A` holds 0, 1, 2 and 3, 25
rows each; an order rule is carried by a derived `D` of 10 beside `A`
0 or 2 and 20 otherwise. Placed in turn: `{D | A}` reading `[[25, 0],
[0, 25], [25, 0], [0, 25]]`, the root `C, E` with every cell 25, then
`A | C` reading `[[25, 0, 25, 0], [0, 25, 0, 25]]`. Every cell is 0 or
at least `f`, and W3 and NE hold; checked on the pairs holding `A`
alone, W1 passes, since `C`'s first band admits `A` at 0 and at 2, two
bands of `A`'s `L2`. But through `{D | A}` that band of `C` admits one
band of `D` only, so "the six absent cells of `C` AND `D` below 15" is
fixed at 6: the full check refuses `A | C` at that level, as it must.
The case is a `K-S6-08` fixture, with the shortcut as its mutant, and
`tests/test_chain_method_page.py` computes it. Lane CHa prices the full
check beside the search.

*Remainder, checked not proven.* None in the table layer beyond (h)'s;
Lemma 3 is exact for the description without slopes and moments.

**(d) Rule words and carried rules.**
- A RULE WORD is a zero of a placed family's table, a published cell
  holding 0: Theorem 1 covers it, and a word that is a function of the
  tables adds nothing to any preimage.
- "Computed" and the phrase are published together, by a drawn step
  whose "not carried" is always eligible, and a carried option is
  eligible under one test read once on the rule's base, which the
  description publishes in either outcome (inventory rows 9, 9b and 10,
  class (a), and the paragraph on every count in (b)). The phrase covers
  0 to `f - 1` failing rows at once, so no word tells 0 from 1 to
  `f - 1`.
- A COMPUTED column publishes no count of its own (4.6b.7's rule: its
  name, place and role only, its absent cells withheld), so no exact cumulative
  count of it exists. A count of its rows below a value `x` is a count
  over `(A, D)`. With the readings free inside their bands, it reaches
  the count of the union of the cells of `A` and `D` whose rows may lie
  below `x`, and Theorem 1 gives that union a table holding at least `f`
  rows unless it holds none in every table; so at the bands the count is
  never bounded inside 1 to `f - 1`. With `A`'s and `D`'s own facts read
  across the two columns (the design's straddle count): CHECKED, NOT
  PROVEN; the design's emergency, lab and stay tables at 20,000 and
  200,000 rows, two seeds each, read 0 of 108 rung intervals inside 1 to
  10.

**(e) Derived columns: the family, its structural zeros and the class.**

*Setting.* An order rule `A <= B` carried by a derived `D`, its option
eligible under rules 1 to 5 of 4.6b.7: the description holds `A`'s
facts, `D`'s one level (edges and totals), the family `{D | A}` with its
structural zeros, the class, and nothing of `B`. The FAILING rows are
those where `D < 0`. The REFINED table is the full joint table of (a)
with the band of `D` holding 0 split by a FAILS mark.

*Lemma 4.* Every count of rows in a union of cells of the refined table
has 0 in its range over the preimage, or reaches `f` in some table of
it.

*Proof.* (i) A count class, `v` at least `f`. Rule 5 makes the cut of
`D`'s level at 0 a floored split: the class publishes `v`, so the parts'
totals are published facts, each 0 or at least `f`. They form one more
family whose one parent is `D`'s band, dealt last in Lemma 1's
construction, so Theorem 1 holds for the refined table, which is (i).
(ii) The phrase class, `v` at most `f - 1`. `D`'s lowest value band
holds at least `max(2 f, f + 4)` rows (rule 1), more than `v`, so its
upper edge lies above 0: were it at or below 0, every row of the band
would fail. So every failing row lies in that band, and each edge's
order statistics, whose ranks are at least that band's count, are no
failing reading. Take any table `T` of the preimage and set each
negative reading of `D` to 0, writing `B` as `A + D` there: `A` is
unchanged, `D`'s readings change only below rank `v + 1`, so its edges
and totals stand, every row keeps its band and so every family keeps its
cells, `B` publishes nothing read from its cells, and the class holds with no failing row;
every draw keeps its eligible options, which read only published facts.
So the preimage holds, beside every table, one with no failing row, and
there a union's count is the count of the band-level union of its HOLDS
cells, which Theorem 1 gives 0 in every table or at least `f` in some.
That is (ii). ∎

*What the rules of 4.6b.7 each close.* Rule 2 publishes the structural
zeros, so that the Corollary of (b) holds for `D` (without them the first
draft's `Omega(D)` held tables no real table makes). Rule 3 floors the
rows where `A` holds a reading and `B` does not, band by band of `A`:
the first review's measurement on 1,000 rows (`A` absent on 15 rows, `B`
on 20, the two overlapping on 13, 10 or 6) read them fixed at 7, 10 or
14 under the first draft. Rule 4 extends RULE W1 to `A`'s own small
groups beside `D`. Rule 5 is (i).

*Finer than the bands.* An edge is interpolated between the two order
statistics either side of its rank (the contract's ranges-class rule),
so each edge PINS at most two order statistics into known bands, at
most four inside one band. The count of a derived column's rows at
values inside one band, alone or crossed with the family, then has an
upper end of at least the band's total less four, at least `f` since
every value band holds `max(2 f, f + 4)` rows, so it is never bounded
inside 1 to `f - 1`. The row 14 example: 1,000 whole-day stays, 195 at
0 days, 7 at 1 and 400 at 2, `p20` = 1 pinning the rows ranked 200 and
201 at 1 day and `p30` = 2: at the deciles the band `[1, 2)` holds 7
rows and that level is not eligible, so no option publishing it can be
drawn. The bound "at most two order statistics an edge" is JUDGEMENT on
the interpolation rule; `K-S6-08`'s fixture of a derived length of stay
on 1,000 rows checks it, with lane MR.

**(f) Structural words.** `exact`, `pinned` and `implied` are functions
of the description (which pairs share a placed family; which
correlations stand), so they add nothing to any preimage. The private
report, with its judged words, is never part of the description: it is
read by the person who ran `synthtwin profile` and holds the real table,
and nothing in it enters a shared file.

**(g) The key, the name, and one description per table.**
- A re-profile of one table under one name and one key, with the same
  settings, the same answers in the questions file and the same
  `procedure` constants, is deterministic, so it publishes the same
  bytes, and a second copy tells nothing.
- A re-profile whose description would differ is refused by the ledger
  unless the person declares, with `--replace-description`, that the
  earlier description was never shared (4.6b.4). An answer that ends a
  hold and makes a column eligible draws new words (the first review
  measured 0 of 39 step words equal before and after), which is the
  two-keys case of stated limit 2 on one installation; another floor or
  another constant draws the same words over other options or weights
  (4.6b.4, corrected by Codex's item 16 of 2026-10-19). Either way the
  two descriptions differ, and the ledger reads the whole protected
  publication, so it sees both cases.
- Two descriptions under one key and two DIFFERENT names draw on words
  whose inputs differ, so in the model of (b) their words are
  independent: the procedure publishes both from a pair of tables
  exactly when it publishes each from its own, and the preimage of the
  pair is the product of the two single preimages. Neither narrows the
  other. MEASURED (plan P4-D407; the design check's four margin sets,
  eight keys, two names): 0 of 29,022 targeted pairs and 0 of 8,000
  sampled pairs leak, and the check's witness cell keeps `[0, 15]` over
  16 tables.
- The ledger refuses the cases the key cannot protect on one
  installation: the same content under another name, under another key,
  or with a different description.
- The stated limit (4.6b.13, limit 2) holds the rest, with its fixtures.

**(h) R1's scope as ruled, and what is proven.**
- **Proven** (Theorem 1 with Lemmas 1 to 4, and the one test's
  sufficient form of 4.6b.7), for a table with ONE row per patient, a
  reader who knows this procedure but not the key, and one description
  per table and name on an installation (R6 as amended), with R1 read
  as R3 reads it and case (ii) of Lemma 3 read as the orchestrator ruled
  on 2026-10-19 ((c)): no count of rows in any union of the full joint
  table's cells, and no count of an own-fact group's rows across
  columns, is fixed at or bounded inside 1 to `f - 1` by the
  description's ladder, chain, family tables, rule words, structural
  words and names (O1 to O3, O7, O8), the census of records holding
  nothing read beside them (RULE WE, the Corollary of (b)); nor by a
  carried rule's class over its base, nor, for an order rule carried by
  a derived column, over the whole description ((e)). The carried
  rules' rows (inventory rows 9, 9b, 10 and 14) are proven on one
  PRECONDITION, open until lane MR's page proves it: that MR's
  inference conditions are implied by the base, the class and the
  antecedent bound, so that every table a carried rule's description
  allows opens the same rule step (Lemma 2; 4.6b.7). "No count" means none beyond each column's
  own facts, which the base product publishes as today, accepted within
  one column (P4-D363); among them a person column's exact repetition
  census while the patient layer is off. What the reading of case (ii)
  accepts is stated as limit 3 (4.6b.13).
- **Checked, not proven:** the slopes (O4: whether a pooled slope adds a
  small count beyond what lane MPOL's witness covers); the moments (lane
  MPOL); the patient layer (lane MG); the straddle count of a computed
  column ((d)); the bound on a derived column's pinned order statistics
  ((e)); a carried rule's class beside the chain's families, for an
  order rule carried by a source column and for a formula rule ((b),
  every count), and beside its base columns' own facts finer than their
  bands (4.6b.7); several carried rules sharing a column beyond the
  step order of 4.6b.7 (the third attack's two-rules table, a `K-S6-08`
  fixture); and the pseudorandom property of keyed BLAKE2b ((b), the
  model).
- **AMENDED by ruling R12 (the orchestrator, 2026-10-20; plan
  P4-D413):** the slopes leave the list above. A slope is published only
  inside a publishing region of section 4.6d, where Theorem 2 of 4.6d.5
  covers it as condition (5) of every point (PROVEN under that section's
  premise (R), but for its exception (i): 4.6d.5 (d) (i) and (h));
  anywhere else it is withheld (4.6b.6, as amended), so no published
  slope stays CHECKED, NOT PROVEN. Reason: the owner's ruling R10,
  strict proof only. Price: the withheld slopes, unmeasured, owed by
  lanes MPp and CHa on lane `E0b`'s battery.
- **Open preconditions:** lane MR's inference conditions, above, for
  rows 9, 9b, 10 and 14.
- **The other three threats.** Identifiers and free text are ineligible
  (4.6b.1). No end of any column is published: every edge, and the
  code's clip, is an interior published rung. Real rows: a twin meeting
  family tables sits closer to the real table than a fresh sample does,
  so `K-S6-05` (whole real rows in the twin, not worse; any rise to the
  owner) is measured at every layer.

#### 4.6b.10 How each argument is checked: `K-S6-08`

**The preimage, as `K-S6-08` counts it.** A table counts as consistent
with a description only where the procedure of this section, run on it
with SOME draw of W5 (every eligible option possible at every step,
4.6b.4), publishes the same description: the same levels, families,
anchors, rule words, structural words, names and, once their pages land,
the same moments and refusals. Matching the published numbers is not
enough (the second red team's N3). On a fixture the enumeration lists
every whole-number table of the fixture's size and every description
each can publish, and a SMALL count leaks where it lies inside 1 to `f -
1` over the whole preimage of a description, fixed or bounded. It runs
at `f` = 11, never at a scaled-down floor, and it enumerates every
description the draw can publish, never only the one a greedy search
would. The key never enters a fixture's expected output.

**Its fixtures for this section** (the design's probes, which lane CHa
brings into the suite; plan P4-D407 gives their measured results):
- the three-way margin scans at `f` = 11, with competing candidates that
  pass the floor, a structural zero in an earlier family and several
  rules on one child; the score-order table and the two-rules table of
  the third attack: 0 leaking descriptions (3,154,474 tables, 7,981
  descriptions);
- W1's part-C example, with W1 as a filter: 0 of 1,030 descriptions
  leak; and the three cases 4.6b.9 (c) adds (a parent cut at `L0` beside
  a band confined below its median; two parents agreeing in one; a
  confinement through a zero of another family), each with the design's
  own clause as the mutant that must leak;
- the F4 cases (the `floor` word; the level choice), the P2 margin sets
  of the W3 and NE scans, and the second red team's P6 (a rule beside
  two families);
- the order-rule tables (emergency visits, laboratory times, stays) of
